answer: Each agent may open only one account per verified hardware key, and the key must sign every transaction and a randomly timed challenge. A challenger can stake tokens to prove two accounts share a key; if the signatures match, the duplicate is frozen and the stake rewards the reporter. This makes identity multiplication require distinct keys and ongoing access to them, not just cheap account creation. An attacker can still buy hardware, but must fund and maintain each identity. Even a wander through opal and juniper markets cannot turn one key into many.
